engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health retained Treya Partners to identify and capture cost-savings across its spend base and to strengthen procurement discipline as part of a private-equity value-creation plan.  The immediate goal is to save roughly $0.7–$1.4 million annually through strategic sourcing while establishing repeatable procurement processes and controls.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project covers 10 spend categories representing about $19 million in annual spend (≈$45 million total company spend, with ≈$19 million deemed addressable).  In-scope categories include Employee Benefits, Medical Devices (IUDs), Diagnostic Devices & Services, Billing Systems/RCM, Medical Supplies, Medical Equipment, Telecom/Data & Voice, Electronic Payment Processing, Data Center/Cloud Hosting, and Office Supplies; the Benefits work-stream is optional and scheduled to start later.  Scope also includes a review of procurement processes/controls, with the understanding that some suppliers or sub-categories may later prove non-addressable.
constraints_challenges: Two separate AP/P-card systems (Mid-Atlantic and Heartland) with limited back-end integration complicate consolidated spend visibility.
Historical line-item usage data is often unavailable; Treya must obtain it directly from high-spend suppliers, and some vendors may not respond despite repeated requests.
Advantia lacks dedicated procurement resources and relies on clinical or operational staff, requiring Treya to minimize client time and manage most sourcing work.
Decentralized, multi-site clinical operations mean strong incumbent supplier relationships and potential resistance to vendor or process changes.
Aggressive project timeline of roughly six months (Benefits stream to follow) requires fast data collection and decision making.

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP data (Oct-2020 – Sep-2021) and YTD P-card data from two systems were available; no centralized contract repository and limited line-item or usage data, which must be sourced from vendors.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Supplier names inconsistent across systems; acquisitions not fully integrated; gaps in usage data common—both parties agreed to proceed once reasonable efforts to obtain data are exhausted.
